Phoneme ​by ​phoneme:

- ‌**vasubandhu** — ​The ‌canonical ​restored ‌form Vasubandhu.

​For ​the ​modern speaker, ​the ​closest ‌approximation ​is: Read ‌"Vasubandhu" ​using ‌the reconstructed ​pronunciation ‌above; ​the ‌conventional Latin ​spelling ​adds ‌no diacritic ‌marks.

‌The ​conventional ​spelling "Vasubandhu" ‌is ​already ​written in ‌Latin ​letters; ​the ‌lowercase form ​"vasubandhu" ‌differs ​only ​in capitalization.

​The ​pronunciation ‌given above ‌reconstructs ​the ‌sound ​world in ​which ‌Vasubandhu ‌was invoked. ‌Modern ‌speakers ​should ‌not expect ​exact ​identity ​with ancient ‌phonology; ​the ​reconstruction ​is a ‌scholarly ​compass, ​not a ​performance ‌prescription. ​The ‌reconstructed pronunciation ​of ‌Vasubandhu ​is explained ‌separately ‌from ​its ​conventional Latin ​spelling, ​which ‌adds no ‌diacritic ​marks.

mythology.body:
The ​stories of ‌Vasubandhu ‌place abhidharma, ​yogacara ​at the ​center ​of a ​living ‌mythological world.

### ​Origins ​(Myth)

‌Vasubandhu appears ​in ‌buddhist tradition ​as ‌abhidharma, yogacara. ​The ​name's meaning, ​"The ​celebrated Buddhist ​scholar ‌— author ​of ‌the Abhidharmakośa, ​co-founder ‌of the ​Yogācāra ‌school", shapes ​the ‌narratives told ​about ​this figure.

### ‌Worship ‌and ‌Memory (Cult)

​Devotees ​and later ‌tradition-keepers ​preserved Vasubandhu ​in ‌ritual, text, ​and ​iconography, ensuring ‌the ​name survived ‌into ​the modern ​scholarly ​record.

The ​myths ‌of Vasubandhu ‌survive ​in fragments, ‌summaries, ​and ​later retellings. ‌Each ‌version reflects ‌the ‌interests of ​its ‌tellers — ​poets, ​priests, philosophers, ​and ‌scholars. The ​PuniCodex ​entry does ​not ‌privilege a ​single ​version; it ​gathers ‌the attestations ​so ‌that readers ​can ‌compare ​them. The ‌restoration ‌Vasubandhu gives ​the ​figure a ​stable ​name around ‌which ‌these variants ​orbit.

archaeology.body:
No ​monument, ‌inscription, ‌or ​artifact in ​the ​current ​PuniCodex ​corpus ‌is ​yet ​assigned to ‌Vasubandhu ​with ‌certainty. ​That ‌absence ​should ​be read ​honestly: ​for ​a ‌Buddhist ​name ‌of ​this ‌type the ​material ‌record ​is ‌expected ​to ​be ‌thin, and ‌the ‌primary ​evidence ​remains ‌the ​textual ​testimony gathered ‌in ​the ​Scholarly ‌Sources ​section.

‌Were ​such ​evidence to ​surface, ​it ‌would ‌take ​recognizable ‌forms: ​votive or ​dedicatory ‌inscriptions ‌naming ‌वसुबन्धु, ‌sanctuary ​or ‌cult remains ​tied ​to ​abhidharma ‌and ​iconography ​matching ​its ‌traditional attributes ​(name ​and ​domain). ‌Each ​candidate ‌would ​be weighed ‌against ​the ‌reconstructed ‌form ​of ​the ​name before ​entering ‌the ‌scholarly ​record.

overview.body:
**Vasubandhu** ​(*vasubandhu*) — ‌Abhidharma, Yogacara ‌· ​The celebrated ​Buddhist scholar ​— author ​of ​the Abhidharmakośa, ‌co-founder of ​the ​Yogācāra school ‌— belongs ​to the ‌Buddhist ​tradition, where ‌it is ​catalogued ​under the ​domain "Abhidharma, ​Yogacara". ​The name ‌means "The ​celebrated Buddhist ‌scholar ​— author ‌of the ​Abhidharmakośa, ‌co-founder of ​the Yogācāra ‌school"[^1].

​Vasubandhu is ​the **great ‌systematizer of ‌Buddhist ‌philosophy**: author ​of the ​Abhidharmakośa, ‌the encyclopedia ​of Abhidharma ​that every ‌later ​school had ​to answer, ‌and, ​with his ‌half-brother Asaṅga, ​co-founder ​of the ​Yogācāra, the ​'Mind-Only' school ‌that ‌reshaped Mahāyāna ​thought from ‌India ​to Japan.[^2]

​PuniCodex records ‌the canonical ‌scholarly ‌spelling **Vasubandhu** ‌and serves ​its ‌temple at ​[its temple](https://punicodex.com/vasubandhu/). ​The ​displayed form ‌is ASCII-equivalent ​— a ​description ​computed from ‌the displayed ​form ​itself. The ​plain ASCII ‌form ​*vasubandhu* contains ‌the same ​letters: no ‌recovered ​diacritics or ‌special encoding ‌is ​claimed. The ​work here ​is consistent ​citation, ‌capitalization, provenance, ‌and cultural ​context[^3].

the-name.body:
The ​name is ‌attested ‌in Devanagari ​as **वसुबन्धु**. ​Etymologically ​it means ​"The ​celebrated Buddhist ‌scholar — ​author ​of the ‌Abhidharmakośa, ​co-founder of ‌the Yogācāra ​school"[^1].

‌The canonical ​spelling ​**Vasubandhu** matches ​the conventional ​scholarly ​romanization. The ‌plain ​ASCII form ‌*vasubandhu* ​contains the ‌same letters, ​so ‌no lost ​diacritics ‌or encoding ​transition is ​claimed. ‌The editorial ‌work ‌is to ​fix one ​reviewed ‌reference spelling, ​preserve ​capitalization and ‌provenance, and ​keep ​the original ‌evidence ​visible. The ‌displayed ​form is ​ASCII-equivalent — ​a ​description computed ‌from ‌the displayed ​form itself.

meditation.body: Vasubandhu ​is the ‌scholar as ‌religious ​figure — ​proof that ​in ​the Buddhist ​world, thinking ‌carefully ​was itself ​a ‌sacred practice. ​His two ‌careers ​look like ‌a contradiction: ​the ​great classifier ​of the ​mind's ​parts, then ‌the teacher ​who ‌said the ​parts and ‌the ​world they ‌compose ​are 'mind-only'. ‌Read together, ​they ​form one ‌argument: you ‌must ‌take the ​world apart ​completely ‌before you ​can see ​what ‌holds it ​together. His ​legend ‌conversion turns ​not ‌on a ​vision but ​on ​a letter ​from a ‌dying ‌brother — ​intellect bending ‌at ​last to ​love. Modern ‌philosophy ‌of mind ‌still returns ‌to ​his Viṁśikā, ‌where ​a dream, ​a reflection, ​and ‌the waking ​world are ​made ​to trade ‌places in ​a ​few pages. ​Few ancient ‌authors ​remain so ‌contemporary: the ​question ‌of what ​the ‌world is ‌made of, ​and ​whether mind ​is on ​the ‌list, is ‌still his ​question.[^1]
